title: Mean-Direction Deflation Reranking for Metric Misuse Repair in Frozen Vector Search

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution frames the training/search metric mismatch as a deployment-time problem for frozen vector search systems. No prior paper explicitly identifies this deployment-time issue for frozen vector search systems. While [6] discusses metric-related issues in vector search, it focuses on the recall metric's relationship to end-to-end system accuracy rather than the specific mismatch problem during deployment. Similarly, [9] and [24] address embedding anisotropy and representation degeneration but do not frame these as deployment-time problems for frozen vector search systems. Thus, no prior paper covers this purpose.

### Mechanism
The contribution analyzes how inner-product search on embeddings trained with normalized metrics degrades on anisotropic embeddings via mean-direction bias and hub vectors. [9] discusses anisotropy in embedding spaces and its impact on similarity measures, including hub effects, which aligns with the mechanism described here. [24] also investigates representation degeneration in embeddings, including issues like narrow cones, which are related to mean-direction bias and hub vectors. Both papers substantively cover the mechanism.

### Evaluation
The contribution uses Iceberg-benchmark evidence to validate the degradation of inner-product search on anisotropic embeddings. [9] employs similar evaluation designs, analyzing embedding anisotropy and its impact on similarity measures using benchmarks and metrics. While the specific benchmark instance (ImageNet-EVA02) differs, the evaluation design — benchmarking embedding degradation and comparing metrics — is substantively equivalent. Thus, the evaluation is covered.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the vector search/dense retrieval deployment domain. [5], [6], [11], and [12] all address vector search and dense retrieval systems, covering this application area. While the specific sub-problem (deployment-time metric mismatch) is new, the general domain of vector search/dense retrieval is well-covered.
